docs.title: EarthBank User Guide
docs.text:
Welcome to the user guide for AuScope EarthBank — an open data platform for the geochemistry community that lets you visualise, synthesise, disseminate, and extract geochemistry data in a global geospatial context.

Looking for the API instead of the platform's own interface? See the EarthBank API documentation.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: I want to... Go to Register an account and get oriented Getting Started Explore or download existing data Finding & Viewing Data Upload my own samples or analytical data Contributing Data Build plots and dashboards from data Visualising Data Access data programmatically API Access Find a citation for a dataset, or cite EarthBank itself References & Citation

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
New to EarthBank? Start here.

  • Registration & accounts — creating a General User account, upgrading to Data Contributor, and managing your account
  • Interface overview — a tour of the Map window, Data window, toolbar, and Help menu

Migration status

This section has been rebranded and reorganised from the original "AusGeochem User Guide 2.0" (Sep 2024). Screenshots are placeholders — see inline [SCREENSHOT: ...] notes — pending fresh captures from the live EarthBank platform.

docs.title: Interface Overview
docs.text:
The EarthBank interface has two primary windows, tied together by the title bar at the top of the page:

  • The Map window — where data is explored geospatially
  • The Data window — where Data Contributors manage their data, and General Users can find and filter publicly available data

Account details are managed from the account menu (see Registration & Accounts); platform help is available from the Help menu (below).

[SCREENSHOT: title bar showing Map window / Data window tabs and account/help icons]

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
The top-left of the Map window has a toolbar for data exploration, visualisation, analysis, and synthesis. Toolbars and pop-up windows on the display can be expanded, collapsed to smaller buttons, or minimised.

[SCREENSHOT: Map window toolbar, expanded state]

docs.title: Help menu
docs.text:
The Help menu (Map window, top right) provides:

Option What it does About Background on the EarthBank platform User Guide Links to this guide How to Cite Citation details for publications that use EarthBank or its archived data — see How to Cite Bug Report Report a bug or defect Feature Request Suggest features or functionality Contact Us Message the AGN/Lithodat development team directly Developer Documentation EarthBank's REST API, for programmatic data inflow and outflow. Full API docs live in a separate repository — see API Access

[SCREENSHOT: Help menu, expanded]

docs.title: Registration & Accounts
docs.text: EarthBank is a bespoke, open data platform for the geochemistry community, developed by the AuScope Geochemistry Network (AGN) and partner Lithodat. It lets users visualise, synthesise, disseminate, and extract geochemistry data in a global geospatial context.

docs.title: Registering as a General User
docs.text: Registering as a General User is quick: provide a name, email address, and password, and accept the EarthBank Terms of Use. General Users can explore, interrogate, and download all publicly visible data on EarthBank, and use the platform's built-in data visualisation and synthesis tools.

docs.title: Upgrading to Data Contributor
docs.text:
To upload data to EarthBank, a General User must first upgrade their account to Data Contributor. This requires providing additional information:

  • Academic, government, or professional institution and role
  • Institutional email address (if not already provided at General User registration)
  • An ORCID iD (free to obtain if you don't already have one)

Data Contributors can upload, disseminate, and publicise data on EarthBank, and browse the data of their institution and its wider community.

docs.title: Managing your account
docs.text:
The account menu (top right of the Map window) is the access point for:

  • Upgrading a General User account to Data Contributor, or checking account status and assigned institution
  • Editing user information — first name, last name, email
  • Changing your EarthBank login password
  • Logging out of the platform

[SCREENSHOT: account menu, expanded, showing the options above]

docs.title: First-time walkthrough
docs.text:
The first time you log in after registering, a pop-up in the Map window highlights featured data collections, useful tools, and short "how to" videos to help you get oriented. It reappears on subsequent logins unless you uncheck the box in its bottom-right corner. You can reopen it at any time from next to the EarthBank logo in the title bar.

[SCREENSHOT: first-time walkthrough pop-up in the Map window]

docs.title: Finding & Viewing Data
docs.text:
General Users can explore, filter, and download all publicly available data on EarthBank without contributing anything themselves.

  • Map window — geospatial exploration, toolbar tools, and filter pop-ups
  • Data window — the Data Packages / Samples / Analytical Data hub
  • Filtering & downloading — filter reference and download options

Screenshots pending

docs.title: The Data Window
docs.text:
The Data window is the hub for browsing, filtering, and downloading samples and their associated data. Open it via the tab at the top right of the Map window. You can also upload data from here — see Contributing Data.

[SCREENSHOT: Data window landing page with left-hand navigation menu]

docs.title: Data landing page
docs.text:
The landing page combines a main content area (defaulting to Start for new users, or Data Packages thereafter) with a left-hand menu:

Section What it's for Start Platform video clips to help new users get oriented quickly Data Packages All Data Packages you can see — public ones, plus any where you're a Team Member. Data Packages are structured collections of data grouped by institution, project, or similar. Owners and Editors can upload, edit, and delete them; anyone can explore, filter, analyse, share, and download public ones. Each Data Package shows its name, description, sample count, analytical data types and volumes, images, files, team members, distribution (Public/Private), workflow state, and DOI — see Data Packages. Contents download as a single ZIP — see Filtering & Downloading Samples Individual samples and their metadata, filterable at the sample level. Clicking a sample opens its landing page with further metadata and download options. Data Package owners/Editors can also add analytical data to a sample from here, via the relevant Add … Data option Analytical Data Geochemical/geochronological data for individual samples, browsable by data type Meta Data (This section was still a placeholder in the source manual — to fill in once confirmed with the team) Shared Data Cross-sample reference data: People, Literature, Funding, Archives, Reference Material, Rocks/Minerals, Labs, and Machines/Instruments

[SCREENSHOT: Data Packages list view, distribution mode]

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Samples can be filtered at the Data Package scale or the individual sample scale, both from the Data window.

Data Package scale — select Data Packages in the left-hand menu. Default filters (Data Package Name, Kind of Data, Institution, Team Member) sit at the top of the window; click the filter icon (top right) for additional options (Distribution, Workflow State, My Team's). Selected filters appear as fields in the header and can be removed with the × next to each.

Sample scale — select Samples (filter by metadata) or Analytical Data (filter by analytical data) in the left-hand menu. Default filters are Sample Name, Data Package, Material, Tag; the filter icon adds Image, IGSN, Creator, Editor, Sample Method, Archive, Literature, Funding, and Person.

[SCREENSHOT: Samples window with filter panel expanded]

docs.title: Filter reference
docs.text: Filter Meaning Package Name Search for a specific Data Package Kind of Data Analytical data type (major/trace geochemistry, fission track, U-Pb geochronology, etc.) Institution Data Contributor's institution Team Member Collaborator granted access to a Data Package Distribution Public or Private Workflow State In Progress, Finished, or Frozen My Team's Toggle to show only Data Packages you created or are a Team Member of Sample Name Search for a specific sample name Material Broad-to-specific classification, e.g. Igneous rock → Granite → zircon Tag User-entered or auto-added at upload With Images Toggle samples that include images IGSN Search by International Generic Sample Number Creator / Editor Find samples by the researcher who created or edited them Sample Method e.g. Hand Sample vs. Core Archive Filter by holding institution Literature Find samples linked to a specific publication Funding Find samples collected under a specific funding scheme Person Search by contributor

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
EarthBank supports three download scopes: a whole Data Package, a single sample, or a selection of samples.

Whole Data Package (ZIP): in Data Packages, click the download icon at the bottom left of the package. A pop-up shows whether a ZIP already exists, its generation date, and whether it's current, with a button to download immediately. The same pop-up's overflow menu lets you generate a fresh ZIP or view ZIP history. If no ZIP has ever been generated, you'll be prompted to create one — you'll get an email when it's ready. The ZIP contains all sample metadata, analytical data, and relevant shapefiles.

[SCREENSHOT: Data Package download pop-up]

Single sample or selection: in Samples or Analytical Data, tick the checkbox next to the sample(s) you want, then use the download button at the top of the window. You can also download the selected samples' shapefile or IGSN QR codes from the same toolbar.

docs.title: Data visibility on the map
docs.text: To control which Data Packages show on the map, go to Data Packages in the Data window and toggle the visibility icon at the bottom left of the package. The title bar's map icon blinks as a reminder to switch back to the Map window to see the change.

docs.title: The Map Window
docs.text:
The global geospatial database can be explored much like Google Maps: click and drag to pan, use the on-screen +/- buttons, the scroll wheel, or a trackpad pinch to zoom, and hold Ctrl while dragging to change the viewing angle.

Click a sample locality to retrieve that sample's metadata and geochemical data. To view and synthesise several samples at once, use the Select Area tool (below). Selecting one or more samples opens a data pop-up with a dropdown for switching between data dashboards — synthetic plots, detailed tables, and a list of associated references, all downloadable.

General Users can view, analyse, and synthesise sample metadata and geochemistry data from the Map window using the toolbar on the left-hand side:

[SCREENSHOT: Map window with left-hand toolbar labelled]

docs.title: Toolbar tools
docs.text:
Data Packages — view, hide, or add Data Packages to the map.

Analytical Layers — filter samples by data type (Samples, Geochemistry, Geochronology, Thermochronology). The toolbar options change depending on which layer is active.

Basemaps — switch between satellite, streets, dark/light themes, topography, bathymetry, and geology, plus Australia-specific overlays (magnetics, gravity, U/Th/K concentrations, soil depth, acid sulphate soils). Any base layer can be shown with or without contour lines.

Select Area — select multiple data points within a region, three ways:

  • Polygon select: click multiple points, then click the first point again (or double-click) to close the shape.
  • Square select: click a start point and drag to size, then click again to complete.
  • Multi-select: as square select, but hold Shift and repeat to define several separate square areas at once.

Go to location — jump to a specific latitude/longitude.

Find — search by sample ID, rock or mineral type, or analysed mineral.

Paleo Reconstructions — view samples in a paleogeographic context. Activating this tool switches the Map window to a paleogeographic basemap with its own toolbar across the top. Available reconstruction models are chosen from a dropdown on the right of that toolbar; a scroll bar at the top toggles the reconstruction age. Some models support a paleotopography overlay; enabling it displays only samples with age information and filters out analytical data younger than the reconstruction age. An interactive present-day pop-up shows where the displayed samples actually sit today, for easy navigation regardless of reconstruction age. The Contour Data and Swath Profile tools, and all filters, continue to work while Paleo Reconstruction is active.

[SCREENSHOT: Paleo Reconstruction toolbar with model dropdown and age scroll bar]

Contour Data — produce a contour profile for a region, based on elevation or any available analytical data. Follow the prompts in the tool's pop-up window.

Swath Profile — investigate the relationship between a selected attribute and topography along a transect. After activating the tool, set the profile width, then click two points on the map to define the transect. Drag the larger of the two green circles to adjust the angle. Click Draw in the pop-up to generate the profile (re-click Draw after any change to refresh it); adjust width with the +/- controls; choose the attribute to colour by (e.g. Age, Fission Track Length) from the dropdown at the bottom left of the profile window; export the profile as an SVG at any time.

[SCREENSHOT: Swath Profile transect and resulting profile plot]

Map View / Global View — toggle between a flat map and a 3D globe.

docs.title: Filter pop-ups
docs.text:
Several toolbar buttons open a filter pop-up on the right side of the Map window. Most support colouring samples by a chosen attribute (via a palette/gradient control) as well as filtering:

Filter Available when What it does Location Type Always Filter/colour by sampling location (Outcrop, Boulder, Section, Mine, Borehole, etc.) via toggles Rock Type Always Filter/colour by rock type (Igneous, Sedimentary, Metamorphic, Ore, Meteorite) via toggles Elevation Always Filter by elevation (–8500 m to 10000 m) via sliders Oxide Geochemistry layer Filter by oxide concentration via sliders; colour-code by a chosen oxide; option to show out-of-range samples as grey outlines Element Geochemistry layer Filter by trace element concentration via sliders; colour-code by a chosen element; same grey-outline option Analysis Scale Geochemistry or Geochronology layer Filter/colour by analytical scale (Whole Rock, Multi-Grain Aliquot, Single Grain, Spot) Mineral Geochemistry layer Filter/colour by analysed mineral (Apatite, Titanite, Zircon, etc.) Analysis Type U-Pb Geochronology layer Filter/colour by analytical method Age Thermochronology or Geochronology layer Colour by measured age (central/pooled age for Fission Track, FT-corrected age for (U-Th)/He), on a geologic-time-scale colour bar; slider filters the age range IQR (U-Th)/He Thermochronology layer Colour by interquartile range of single-grain ages — a dispersion indicator where low IQR implies less scatter Technique Fission Track Thermochronology layer Filter/colour by measurement technique Track Length Fission Track Thermochronology layer Colour by mean track length (MTL, µm); slider filters the range Track Length σ Fission Track Thermochronology layer Colour by 1σ standard deviation of MTL; slider filters unimodal vs. broad/bimodal distributions

[SCREENSHOT: example filter pop-up, e.g. Oxide filter with concentration sliders]

docs.title: Contributing Data
docs.text:
To upload anything, first upgrade to a Data Contributor account — see Registration & Accounts.

  • Data packages — the organising unit for every upload
  • Sample metadata — manual or bulk sample entry
  • IGSN minting — persistent sample identifiers
  • DOI minting — citable dataset identifiers
  • Geochemistry data — major & trace element data
  • U-Pb geochronology data
  • (U-Th)/He data
  • Fission track data
  • Thermal history data

Screenshots pending

Text content is migrated and rebranded; screenshots are marked [SCREENSHOT: ...] pending fresh captures from the live platform.

docs.title: Data Packages
docs.text: To upload data, first upgrade your account from General User to Data Contributor — see Registration & Accounts.

docs.title: Why Data Packages exist
docs.text: All data in EarthBank is uploaded in a structured, relational way so it can be queried, synthesised, and visualised on the fly. Sample metadata, Fission Track data, and every other data type are each uploaded through their own template and drag-and-drop box, but they all attach back to samples grouped under a Data Package — the organising unit for a dataset. Keeping data structured this way also makes it possible to link new analytical data to samples already on the platform.

docs.title: Creating a Data Package
docs.text:
1. In the title bar, open Data, then select Data Packages from the left-hand menu.
  2. Click + New (top right corner).
  3. Enter a name and click Save — you'll land on the Data Package's property setup page.

From here you can set package information, add team members, attach files/images, and mint a DOI (DOI Minting).

[SCREENSHOT: Data Package property setup page, Package Info tab]

docs.title: Package information
docs.text:
On the Package Info tab, set:

  • Name and Description — the description appears on the map when hovering over the Data Package's info icon
  • Distribution — Public or Private (see below)
  • Workflow State — In Progress, Finished, or Frozen (see below)
  • License

docs.title: Data privacy control
docs.text:
Distribution controls who can see a Data Package's data:

  • Public — visible to the whole EarthBank community
  • Private — visible only to designated Team Members (see below), for a limited embargo period

EarthBank is designed as an open repository, so Private data defaults to a two-year embargo from upload date. Data already in the public domain (e.g. published in a journal) must be uploaded as Public.

Before the two-year embargo ends, you'll be notified that the data will automatically switch to Public. At that point you can request a one-year extension, granted automatically, and a further extension after that (four years total). After four years, any data still Private is made Public automatically.

You can also switch a package to Public manually at any time: open Data Packages, click the package's overflow menu, open the Package Info tab, select Public from the Distribution dropdown, and save.

docs.title: DOI workflow state
docs.text:
Also on the Package Info tab, the Data Contributor (and anyone added as a Supervisor) can set the Workflow State:

State Meaning In Progress Editors can still edit datapoints in the package Finished Datapoints can no longer be edited Frozen The package can no longer be changed at all. Cannot be undone. Only use once a package is DOI-minted and published

Warning

Do not set a Data Package to Frozen before publication.

docs.title: Team members
docs.text:
On the Team tab, add collaborators as Team Members so they can view and edit the Data Package — useful for shared research projects.

[SCREENSHOT: Team tab, adding a collaborator]

docs.title: Attaching files
docs.text: On the Files tab, either create a folder and upload a batch of images/files, or upload directly via the upload icon. Files can be downloaded or deleted at any time from the same tab.

docs.title: DOI Minting
docs.text: EarthBank can generate a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) for a Data Package, giving it a permanent, citable reference and helping datasets meet publication requirements.

docs.title: Minting a DOI
docs.text:
While creating a new Data Package:

  1. Open Data, select Data Packages, click + New.
  2. Name and describe the package, save, then open the DOI tab.
  3. Click Mint to get a DOI instantly.

For an existing Data Package:

  1. Open Data Packages, click the overflow menu on the package, open the DOI tab.
  2. Click Mint, then save.

[SCREENSHOT: DOI tab with Mint button]

While you're there, you can also set Distribution (Public/Private) and Workflow State (In Progress/Finished/Frozen) from the Package Info tab — see Data Packages and Data Packages for what each means.

docs.title: Contributing Fission Track Data
docs.text:
EarthBank curates fission track (FT) age and length data at both the sample and single-grain level, accepting Population Method, EDM, LA-ICP-MS, and ζ-calibration methodologies. As with other data types: manual entry sample-by-sample, or bulk upload via Excel (recommended for multi-sample datasets with many single-grain results).

Get there via Data → Analytical Data → Fission Track.

docs.title: Manual entry
docs.text:
1. Click + New, choose the Data Package, then Create.
  2. Work through the tabs: Fission Track Datapoint, Fission Track Data, Single Grain FT Data, Length Data (unique to this data model), plus the platform-wide More and Files tabs.

docs.title: Fission Track Datapoint tab
docs.text: Mark the sample as unknown or reference material. The Batch ID links unknowns to the reference material measured with them (same convention as (U-Th)/He — see Contributing (U-Th)/He Data). Fields are mostly predefined dropdowns.

docs.title: Fission Track Data tab
docs.text: Multi-grain summary data: number of grains measured, pooled/central age, mean U content, dosimeter used, mean kinetic results. If a dropdown (e.g. Dosimeter) is missing an option you need, use Help → Contact Us.

docs.title: Single Grain FT Data tab
docs.text: Add single-grain count data and/or single-grain age data via the relevant radio button and + New, or upload a CSV (separate templates exist for count data and age data — expand Batch Edit to download/upload). In each CSV, DataPointName must exactly match the sample name set in the Fission Track Datapoint tab.

docs.title: Length Data tab
docs.text: Add track length data via one of two radio-button-selected formats, or by CSV (separate templates for Individual Track Lengths and Binned Lengths — expand Batch Edit). Seven additional summary fields at the top right (mean track length / MTL, total tracks measured, etc.) can be filled even without individual lengths — useful for legacy data reporting only mean results.

docs.title: More & Files tabs
docs.text:
Same pattern as elsewhere: More links collaborators/publications; Files takes raw data, grain images, drawings, or figures.

Once complete, return to the Fission Track Datapoint tab and save.

[SCREENSHOT: Fission Track Datapoint tabs]

docs.title: Excel Wizard (bulk upload)
docs.text:
Download the blank .XLSX template from the bottom of the Fission Track window.

Sheet Purpose FT Datapoints One row per sample; reference-material rows via Secondary Reference Material dropdown, linked to unknowns by matching Batch ID FTCountData Mean counting data: pooled/central age, grains measured, mean Dpar FTSingleGrain Single-grain counting data: ages, U content FTLengthData / FTBinnedLengthData Track length measurements — pick the sheet matching your data format

Warning

Don't touch the first 4 rows — the platform reads them on upload.

Key / Datapoint Key example

For sample FtNsw-03 with 20 single-grain ages, set Key = FtNsw-03_B in FT Datapoints, then repeat FtNsw-03_B as Datapoint Key in FTCountData, FTSingleGrain, and FTLengthData/FTBinnedLengthData.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
1. Save the template, drag it into the drop box (or click to browse).
  2. Fix any flagged issues (missing headers, unlinked Keys), then click Proceed.
  3. Choose the destination Data Package, click Next (or Cancel to edit the file directly).
  4. Step through the wizard's 3 validation steps, then click Upload Batch to finalise.

Warning

Data isn't live until Upload Batch is pressed.

docs.title: Contributing Major & Trace Geochemistry Data
docs.text:
Major and trace geochemistry data can be added by manual entry or, for anything but the smallest datasets, via the Excel Wizard (recommended — manual entry is slow and error-prone at scale).

Get there via Data → Analytical Data → Geochemistry.

docs.title: Manual entry
docs.text:
1. Click + New to create an inorganic geochemistry datapoint, choose the Data Package, then Create.
  2. Fill in general datapoint info (analytical technique, mineral analysed, sample name), then save.
  3. Go to the analytical data tab and enter the U-Pb-style analytical data.

The following are optional but recommended where available:

  1. Intra-sample/aliquot details (grain/aliquot ID, spot ID, grain domain, total wt% of analysis)
  2. Oxide concentrations and uncertainty per aliquot/grain/spot
  3. Element concentrations, uncertainty, and measured mass per aliquot/grain/spot

docs.title: Excel Wizard
docs.text:
Download the blank GCDatapoint template from the drag-and-drop box at the bottom of the Geochemistry window. It contains:

Sheet Purpose GC Datapoints One row per sample (or per secondary reference material — use the Sec. Reference Material column for those, one row each). Records sample name, mineral analysed, and metadata (analytical method, lab, analyst) GC Concentrations One row per analysis/spot: concentrations, uncertainties, measured masses. Linked back to GC Datapoints via the Key/Datapoint Key pair Column Descriptions Reference only Lookup Tables Backing lists — don't edit

Warning

Red columns are required. Other columns can be reordered or deleted. Don't touch the first 4 rows.

Key / Datapoint Key

The Key (set in GC Datapoints) is a unique value you assign per sample or reference material. Every related row in GC Concentrations repeats that same value in its Datapoint Key column, linking spot/grain-level data back to the sample.

Important: only fill Sec. Reference Material for actual reference-material rows — link unknowns to reference material via matching Analytical ID, not this column.

docs.title: Detection limits
docs.text: Below a known numerical detection limit: prefix the value with < (e.g. <0.01). Below an unspecified limit: enter just <.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
1. Save the completed template, then drag it into the drop box on the Geochemistry window (or click to browse).
  2. Choose the destination Data Package.
  3. Step through the validation windows left to right — each flags Errors (block upload until fixed) and Warnings (should be reviewed).
  4. Once every window is clear, click Upload.
  5. Click the final confirmation button to finalise the import.

[SCREENSHOT: Excel Wizard batch validation table with errors/warnings]

Warning

Data isn't live until you click the final Upload Batch button.

docs.title: IGSN Minting
docs.text:
Data Contributors are strongly encouraged to mint an International Generic Sample Number (IGSN) for every geosample they upload. As the IGSN e.V. non-profit puts it:

The application and long-term utility of sample based data is critically dependent on availability of information (metadata) about the samples, links to other data sets derived from individual samples, and access to the samples themselves... Using persistent identifiers for physical samples, such as the International Geo Sample Number (IGSN), provides solutions. The IGSN ID is a globally unique, persistent, domain-agnostic identifier for material samples.

docs.title: Minting an IGSN for one sample
docs.text:
Available either while creating/uploading a sample, or later, via the sample's IGSN tab. If the sample already has an IGSN, enter it manually. Otherwise, click Mint to open the Minting IGSNs pop-up:

Field Meaning Sample Name The sample name/ID you provided during upload Namespace Set for the whole platform via the minting DataCite member (Lithodat) Proposed IGSN ID Auto-suggested; you can instead specify your own 6–12 character string of capital letters and numbers (no spaces) — but auto-generation is recommended

[SCREENSHOT: Minting IGSNs pop-up]

docs.title: Minting IGSNs for multiple samples
docs.text:
1. Open Data, select Samples.
  2. Tick the checkboxes for the samples you want to mint.
  3. Click Batch Mint.
  4. The same Minting IGSNs pop-up appears as above.

Every minted sample gets a dedicated webpage, QR code, and citable DOI.

docs.title: Contributing Sample Metadata
docs.text: Sample metadata can be added one sample at a time, or in bulk via an Excel template. For anything beyond a handful of samples, use the Excel Wizard.

docs.title: Manual entry (individual samples)
docs.text:
1. In the title bar, open Data, select Samples from the left-hand menu, then click + New (top right).
  2. Enter the Sample Name, choose the Data Package it belongs to (create one first if needed — see Data Packages), and continue.
  3. Work through the tabs below, saving between each.

[SCREENSHOT: new sample creation window, Sample tab]

docs.title: Sample tab
docs.text: Field Notes Sample Name — Data Package Must already exist Stratigraphic Unit Dropdown, or add a new one via the + icon Sample Kind Dropdown Sampling Method Dropdown Rock/Mineral Dropdown, backed by mindat.org Sample Age [Ma] Single value or range Collection date Single value or range Notes on Sample / Notes on Archive Free text Archive Current storage location — dropdown, or add new via + Tags User-defined, improve searchability

docs.title: Location tab
docs.text: Field Notes Location Name — Location Kind Dropdown Note on Location Free text Use this location Pick a point on the interactive map (street or satellite view) Latitude / Longitude WGS84 Location Accuracy Estimated Elevation On Surface or Below Surface; auto-filled from lat/long if left blank; reference elevation type set under Advanced elevation

docs.title: IGSN tab
docs.text: See IGSN Minting.

docs.title: Metadata links tab
docs.text: Field Notes Involved People + Link Person, then choose from the dropdown or add a new entry via +; role can be added Referenced Literature + Link Literature, then choose from the dropdown or add via DOI or manually Funding + Link Funding, then choose from the dropdown or add via +; notes optional Properties Free-form key/value pairs for anything not covered elsewhere, e.g. colour=brown, weight(gram)=34

docs.title: Files tab
docs.text: Upload images or related files individually or as a folder.

docs.title: Batch upload (Excel Wizard)
docs.text:
For uploading many samples at once:

  1. Open Data, select Samples, scroll to the bottom of the page, and download the Sample metadata Excel template from the drag-and-drop box.
  2. Fill it in (see below), then drag it back into that same box (or click to browse).

[SCREENSHOT: Sample metadata drag-and-drop upload box]

The template has three sheets:

Sheet Purpose Samples Enter data here. Required fields are highlighted pink, highly recommended yellow, optional green. The first two rows describe each field Column Descriptions Reference only — column names and definitions. Don't edit Lookup Tables Backing lists for the Samples sheet's dropdowns

Warning

Don't change the first 4 rows of the template — the platform reads them on upload.

docs.title: Upload steps
docs.text:
1. Drop the completed file into the upload box. The platform validates it and shows a prompt — errors must be fixed before continuing (exit via the close icon, fix the file, try again); a green prompt means you're clear to proceed.
  2. Choose the destination Data Package.
  3. You'll land on a batch-editing table flagging any remaining errors/warnings, sortable by either. Use set new value in all empty cells (after selecting one empty cell) to bulk-fill. You can export the table as CSV at any point.
  4. Once there are no errors or warnings left, click Upload. A success prompt reports how many rows were imported.
  5. Click through to finish — the final prompt shows the tag name applied to the imported batch.

docs.title: Contributing Thermal History Data
docs.text:
EarthBank stores thermal history model data — predicted results and time-temperature (tT) reconstruction points — from any modelling software, for both single-sample models and multi-sample models (e.g. vertical transects, boreholes). Thermal history data can be linked to existing samples, Fission Track data, (U-Th)/He data, geochemistry data, and U-Pb data, so measured and model-predicted results can be compared directly.

Get there via Data → Analytical Data → Thermal History. As elsewhere, you can build a model manually or (strongly recommended) bulk-upload via Excel.

docs.title: Model-by-model (manual) entry
docs.text:
1. Click + New, choose the Data Package, then Create.
  2. Work through the tabs: General, tT Sample, tT Input, tT Model Constraint, tT Path (unique to this data model), plus the platform-wide More and Files tabs.

docs.title: General tab
docs.text: Define the model set-up: software used, approach, iterations, starting temperature gradient.

docs.title: tT Sample tab
docs.text: Click + New to link the model to a sample. Give it a Name — a unique identifier, ideally related to the sample name (e.g. sample T1-05 → name T1-05-model). This name is used to reference the model in later tabs.

docs.title: tT Input tab
docs.text: Click + New to add a THistInput datapoint. Set Thermal History to the name from the previous tab. Fill in the constraint fields as applicable, and enter the model-predicted results (age, track length, or reflectance) at the bottom — if measured Fission Track or (U-Th)/He data for the sample is already on the platform, this lets it be compared directly against the model. Repeat + New for additional inputs if the model uses multiple data types as constraints.

docs.title: tT Model Constraint tab
docs.text: Click + New to define a time-temperature constraint box (mean and range of both time and temperature), with a Constraint Type dropdown. Repeat for multiple constraints — e.g. a present-day constraint is set as time = 0, range = 0, with Constraint Type = Present-day.

docs.title: tT Path tab
docs.text:
Click + New to add a THistNickpoint — a point in time-temperature space along the model path. Since most modelling software doesn't export path data directly, points usually need digitising from a figure first (the team recommends WebPlotDigitizer). For more than a couple of points, use the CSV batch option instead: expand Batch Edit to download/upload a CSV, where datapointName must exactly match the name set in the tT Sample tab.

Tip

Adding path points one at a time is slow — use the bulk Excel uploader below for anything beyond a trivial model.

docs.title: More & Files tabs
docs.text:
Same pattern as elsewhere.

Once complete, return to the General tab and save.

docs.title: Bulk upload (Excel Wizard)
docs.text:
Two templates are available at the bottom of the Thermal History window:

  • THDatapoint_SingleSample.template.xlsx — single-sample models only
  • THDatapoint_MultiSample.template.xlsx — single- or multi-sample models (has extra fields; use only when you actually need multi-sample support)

Either template can carry multiple models in one file — no need for a separate upload per model iteration.

Key / Datapoint Key

The Key is set in the tT Model Setup sheet, uniquely identifying a sample and/or model iteration (e.g. FT-102-model). Every related row in the other sheets repeats that value as Datapoint Key. For multi-sample models, use a generic key for the model as a whole (e.g. model_transect_A), repeated across all the samples that belong to it.

docs.title: Single-sample template
docs.text:
Four sheets:

Sheet Purpose tT Model Setup Model metadata, starting parameters, and the Key tT InputOutput Data used to constrain the model, and the model's predicted age/track length/reflectance output; links to existing sample data already on the platform tT Model Constraint Time-temperature constraint box(es) — mean and range of time and temperature; present-day constraint uses time = 0, range = 0, Constraint Type = Present-day tT Path The digitised time-temperature path points (see WebPlotDigitizer note above)

docs.title: Multi-sample template
docs.text:
Same four sheets, plus:

Sheet Purpose tT Sample Links multiple samples to one model — one row per sample, Datapoint Key matching the model's Key

The remaining sheets work as in the single-sample template, except tT Path additionally records which sample each path belongs to, and tT InputOutput may have multiple constraint rows per sample — keep Datapoint Keys (and Sample Names, where multiple constraints share a sample) matched carefully.

Warning

Don't touch the first 4 rows of either template — the platform reads them on upload.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
1. Save the completed template, drag it into the drop box at the bottom of the Thermal History window (or click to browse).
  2. Fix any flagged issues (missing headers, unlinked Keys), then click Proceed.
  3. Choose the destination Data Package, click Next (or Cancel to edit the file directly).
  4. Step through the wizard's 3 validation steps, then click Upload Batch to finalise.

[SCREENSHOT: Thermal history bulk upload validation steps]

Warning

Data isn't live until Upload Batch is pressed.

docs.title: Contributing U-Pb(-Th) Geochronology Data
docs.text:
EarthBank accepts U-Pb(-Th) data from Thermal Ionisation Mass Spectrometry (TIMS), in-situ Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS/SHRIMP), and in-situ Laser Ablation ICP-MS (LA-ICP-MS, LA-MC-ICP-MS), each with its own bulk-upload template.

Get there via Data → Analytical Data → U-Pb.

There are two upload routes: manual entry (slow, error-prone — least recommended) or bulk upload via Excel templates, Excel Wizards, CSV importers, or third-party uploaders (e.g. SQUID 3) — the recommended route.

Note

Data can only be uploaded to an existing sample belonging to an existing Data Package — see Sample Metadata and Data Packages.

docs.title: Manual entry
docs.text:
1. Click + New, choose the Data Package, then Create to start a new U-Pb datapoint.
  2. Fill in general info (analytical technique, sample or secondary reference material, sample name), then save.
  3. Go to the analytical data tab, and enter the U-Pb data.

Optional but recommended if available:

  • Age grouping (e.g. crystallisation age, max deposition age) and calculation method (e.g. weighted mean ²⁰⁶Pb/²³⁸U, concordia age)
  • Analytical metadata (instrument model, analytical conditions, calibration strategies)

docs.title: Excel Wizard
docs.text:
Several templates are available depending on acquisition method — download the one matching your data from the U-Pb window. Each has three main sheets:

Sheet Purpose UPb Datapoints One row per sample (or per secondary reference material, e.g. one row for Temora, one for Mud Tank). Records sample name, mineral analysed, and metadata UPbSpotDatap One row per analysis/spot: concentrations, ratios, dates. Linked to UPb Datapoints via Key/Datapoint Key UPbAgeGroup Optional — records interpreted ages (as opposed to raw dates), where statistical grouping has already been applied. Also linked via Datapoint Key Column Descriptions / Lookup Tables Reference only — don't edit Lookup Tables

Warning

Don't touch the first 4 rows — the platform reads them on upload.

Important: only fill Sec. Reference Material for actual reference-material rows — link unknowns to reference material via matching Batch ID.

Key / Datapoint Key example

For sample AUS-12 with 30 zircon spots, set Key = AUS-12_A in UPb Datapoints. Use AUS-12_A as the Datapoint Key for all 30 rows in UPbSpotDatap, and again for any derived age groups in UPbAgeGroup.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
1. Save the template, then drag it into the drop box at the bottom of the U-Pb window (or click to browse).
  2. If issues are found, fix and retry; a green prompt means you're clear — click Proceed.
  3. Choose the destination Data Package, click Next.
  4. A summary lists each uploaded table (U-Pb datapoints, spot data, age groups). Open each in turn, review/fix any flagged errors or warnings, and confirm — repeat until every table shows a green check and "Successfully Imported".
  5. Click the final Upload Batch button to finalise.

[SCREENSHOT: table-by-table import review with green checkmarks]

Warning

Data isn't live until Upload Batch is pressed.

docs.title: Contributing (U-Th)/He Data
docs.text:
EarthBank handles both whole-grain and in-situ (U-Th)/He data from virtually any mineral. As with other data types, upload sample-by-sample (manual) or in bulk via the Excel Wizard — bulk is recommended for complex, multi-sample datasets.

Get there via Data → Analytical Data → (U-Th)/He, then use + New to create data or the upload options at the bottom of the window.

docs.title: Manual entry
docs.text:
1. Click + New, choose the Data Package, then Create.
  2. Work through the tabs below.

docs.title: The Datapoint tab
docs.text:
Covers the sample as a whole (not a single grain): sample name, sample type, mineral analysed, number of aliquots, measured mean data. Save changes with the confirm button in the lower left before moving on. Start by marking the sample as unknown or reference material (e.g. Durango apatite, Fish Canyon zircon).

Batch ID

The Batch ID links unknown samples to the reference material measured alongside them — matching Batch IDs are treated as belonging together (equivalent to Session ID in the LA-ICP-MS data model).

Hover the info icon on any field for more detail. Once complete, continue to Analytical Metadata.

docs.title: Analytical Metadata tab
docs.text: Choose whether the analysis was whole-grain or in-situ — this shows/hides the relevant fields. All fields are predefined dropdowns; if an option you need is missing, use Help → Contact Us in the title bar to flag it.

docs.title: Whole-Grain Analysis / In-Situ Analysis tab
docs.text: Click + New (within the relevant tab) to add a single-grain or multi-grain aliquot — a pop-up opens with fields including measured age, uncertainty, FT correction, and grain dimensions. Not all fields are required. Repeat + New for each additional aliquot.

docs.title: More & Files tabs
docs.text:
More links the datapoint to other platform entities — a collaborating user, a publication, etc. Files accepts anything that doesn't fit a predefined field: raw data, grain images, drawings, figures.

Once done, return to the Datapoint tab and save — the new data appears in the (U-Th)/He list and on the Map window.

[SCREENSHOT: (U-Th)/He datapoint creation, Datapoint tab]

docs.title: Excel Wizard (bulk upload)
docs.text:
Best for datasets with multiple samples and multiple aliquots each. At the bottom of the (U-Th)/He window, choose the Excel Wizard or .CSV uploader option (Excel Wizard recommended) and download the blank .XLSX template.

Sheet Purpose He Datapoints One row per sample. For a reference standard, select it via the Sec. Reference Material dropdown; link to unknowns via matching Batch ID HeWholeGrain / HeInSitu Metadata and calculated mean values, plus per-aliquot results. Both can be used in the same file if you have both data types Column Descriptions / Lookup Tables Reference only

Warning

Don't touch the first 4 rows — the platform reads them on upload.

Important: Sec. Reference Material is only for measured secondary reference material rows, not the reference material used during instrument calibration. Link unknowns to reference results via Batch ID.

Key / Datapoint Key example

For sample HeVic-12 with 5 whole-grain results, set Key = HeVic-12_A in He Datapoints, then repeat HeVic-12_A as the Datapoint Key for each of the 5 rows in HeWholeGrain.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
1. Save the template, drag it into the drop box (or click to browse).
  2. The platform flags issues (missing headers, unlinked Keys) if any — fix and retry.
  3. Choose the destination Data Package, click Next (or Cancel to go back and edit the file directly).
  4. Step through the wizard's 3 validation steps, then click Upload Batch to finalise.

Warning

Data isn't live until Upload Batch is pressed.

docs.title: Visualising Data
docs.text:
Built-in dashboards and plots for each analytical data type:

  • Geochemistry
  • U-Pb geochronology
  • (U-Th)/He thermochronology
  • Fission track

Screenshots pending

Text content is migrated and rebranded; screenshots are marked [SCREENSHOT: ...] pending fresh captures from the live platform.

docs.title: Visualising Fission Track Data
docs.text:
1. Go to the Map window and confirm the relevant Data Package is switched on in the Data Packages panel (top left) — for example, the Australian Thermochronology Compilation.
  2. Open Analytical Layers and select the Fission Track method of interest (e.g. apatite Fission Track).

The map colours sample locations by data type by default. Colour samples instead by Age, Location Type, Rock Type, Elevation, Technique (EDM, LA-ICP-MS), Track Length (mean track length, MTL), or Track Length σ (standard deviation of MTL) via the relevant filter control (see the filter reference).

Hovering a sample shows its name, rock type, elevation, central age and age error, MTL and standard deviation, and technique.

[SCREENSHOT: Fission Track layer active, colour bar set to Track Length]

docs.title: Sample detail
docs.text: Clicking a sample opens a pop-up with detailed sample and Fission Track information, expandable into Sample Data and Analytical Data views. Where multiple samples share a locality, each has its own Sample Data / Analytical Data pair to select. The Analytical Data view includes plots such as a radial plot coloured by uranium concentration.

docs.title: Multi-sample selection
docs.text:
Use the polygon select tool (left toolbar) to draw around samples of interest — left-click to place each anchor point, right-click to close the polygon. The resulting window lists the selected samples and offers a shapefile download.

Switch between sample metadata and Fission Track dashboards via the dropdown at the top left. Each dashboard supports up to eight plot tiles, each independently configurable (data type, axis size, point colour) and exportable.

Use the multi-select tool to compare populations across geographic areas — for example, comparing Boomerang plots (age vs. MTL) across regions of Australia's passive continental margin.

[SCREENSHOT: multi-region Boomerang plot comparison]

Combine with the Paleo Reconstruction and Contour Data tools for further interpretation.

docs.title: Visualising Major & Trace Geochemical Data
docs.text:
Geochemistry data is visualised directly in the Map window.

  1. Open Analytical Layers and tick Geochemistry to enable geochemistry functionality.
  2. Filter by Location Type, Rock Type, Analysis Scale, and Mineral as needed.
  3. Use the Oxide and Element filters to filter by concentration via sliders, and colour samples by a chosen oxide/element using the dropdown at the top of the panel. Samples outside the selected range are hidden by default — enable show out-of-range to display them as empty circles instead.

[SCREENSHOT: Geochemistry Analytical Layer active, Oxide filter panel]

docs.title: Interpolation maps
docs.text: Under Tools, the interpolation tool lets you select an area (via the area select tool) and generate an interpolated concentration map for a chosen oxide or element across that area.

docs.title: Plotting multiple samples
docs.text:
1. Select samples using Select Area — a rectangle, polygon, or multi-select (see The Map Window) — to open the selections tab.
  2. Optionally assign samples to specific populations via the dropdown in the selections tab.
  3. Open Geochemistry from the plotting dropdown to launch the plotting window, with samples coloured by population.
  4. Choose how many plot tiles to show, and set each tile's plot type and axes via its dropdowns.
  5. Export any tile via its export button, choosing a file format.

[SCREENSHOT: multi-sample geochemistry plotting window with population colouring]

docs.title: On the map
docs.text:
1. Open Analytical Layers and tick U-Pb to enable geochronology functionality.
  2. Filter by location type, rock type, and analysis type, or by age using the colour-coded slider at the base of the map. The palette control lets you change the colour gradient used.

Under Tools, the interpolation tool creates an age interpolation map for a selected area; the Paleo Reconstruction tool (see The Map Window) shows samples in their paleogeographic context.

docs.title: Individual sample view
docs.text:
Clicking an individual sample (in geochronology mode) opens a pop-up with:

  • A sample metadata summary table
  • A geochronology data summary table
  • Plots for that sample, scalable and exportable (JPEG, PNG, SVG, PDF) via the tile's controls, including: Wetherill plots, Tera-Wasserburg plots, weighted mean of the preferred isotopic date, histograms (preferred date, Th/U, U concentration), kernel density estimates, bivariate plots (isotopic ratios, dates, major/trace concentrations, Th/U), and radial plots

[SCREENSHOT: individual sample pop-up with Wetherill/Tera-Wasserburg plots]

docs.title: Multi-sample selection
docs.text:
1. Select samples using Select Area — rectangle, polygon, or multi-select — to open the selections tab.
  2. Optionally assign samples to populations via the dropdown.
  3. Open U-Pb from the plotting dropdown to launch the plotting window, coloured by population.
  4. Choose the number of plot tiles and set each tile's type/axes.
  5. Export any tile via its export button.

docs.title: Visualising (U-Th)/He Data
docs.text:
1. Go to the Map window and confirm the relevant Data Package is switched on in the Data Packages panel (top left). If it's not listed, open Data Packages to browse and enable one — for example, the Australian Thermochronology Compilation.
  2. Open Analytical Layers and select the (U-Th)/He method of interest (e.g. apatite (U-Th)/He only).

[SCREENSHOT: Map window filtered to (U-Th)/He data, Analytical Layers panel open]

Colour samples by Rock Type, Location Type, Elevation, Age, or Interquartile Range (IQR) via the relevant filter control (see the filter reference).

Hovering a sample shows its name, rock type, elevation, mean corrected age, and corrected age error. Clicking a sample opens detailed sample and (U-Th)/He information, including plots such as eU vs. Corrected Single Grain Age. The sample can be exported as a shapefile with all its (U-Th)/He data.

docs.title: Multi-sample selection
docs.text:
Use the polygon select tool (left toolbar) to draw around samples of interest — left-click to place each anchor point, right-click to close the polygon. The resulting selection window lists all samples in the polygon and can be downloaded as a shapefile for use in other GIS software.

Switch between sample metadata and analytical data dashboards via the dropdown at the top left of the window. Each dashboard supports up to eight plot tiles; each tile has its own display and control settings (data type, axis size, point colour).

Plots are publication-ready and export via each tile's export control. Use the multi-select tool to define separate populations and compare trends across the dataset — for example, comparing sectors coloured by location.

[SCREENSHOT: (U-Th)/He multi-sample dashboard with population comparison]

docs.title: API Access
docs.text:
EarthBank provides a REST API so external software, scripts, and systems can read and write EarthBank-hosted data — for example, automated metadata upload from a lab's own systems, scripted data retrieval, or feeding EarthBank data into downstream synthesis and machine-learning workflows.

Full API documentation — authentication, endpoints, worked examples for reading and writing data — lives in a dedicated repository rather than here, so it can be maintained by and for developers without duplicating content:

→ io.lithosurfer.userdoc

Interactive (Swagger) API documentation is also available directly from the platform's Help menu once you're a registered Data Contributor.

docs.title: References & Citation
docs.text:
• Finding data references — locating the literature reference behind a sample or dataset
  • How to cite — citing EarthBank itself in your publications

docs.title: Finding Data References
docs.text: References for data on EarthBank can be found at the individual sample scale from either the Map window or the Data window.

docs.title: From the Map window
docs.text:
Select or filter samples as described in Finding & Viewing Data. Once a sample is displayed, click it to open the sample information pop-up. If multiple samples share a location, a selection window opens first — click the sample ID you want to open its sample information window. The literature reference appears in a dropdown within that window, usually as a clickable link to the publication.

[SCREENSHOT: sample information pop-up with literature reference dropdown]

docs.title: From the Data window
docs.text:
Open the Data tab, select Samples from the left-hand menu, then search or filter (see Filtering & downloading) to find the sample you want. Click its row to open the sample landing page, where the data reference is a clickable link through to the literature window with further publication details.

[SCREENSHOT: sample landing page with literature reference link]

docs.title: How to Cite
docs.text: Publications and reports that benefit from the use of EarthBank and its archived data should reference the following.

docs.title: General platform use
docs.text:
For general use of the platform, cite:

Boone, S.C., Dalton, H., Prent, A., Kohlmann, F., Theile, M., Gréau, Y., Florin, G., Noble, W., Hodgekiss, S.A., Ware, B. and Phillips, D., 2022. AusGeochem: An Open Platform for Geochemical Data Preservation, Dissemination and Synthesis. Geostandards and Geoanalytical Research, 46(2), pp.245-259. doi: 10.1111/ggr.12419. Open access.

docs.title: Thermochronology work
docs.text:
For work using thermochronology data (fission track, (U-Th)/He, and thermal history models) and associated analytical tools, also cite:

Boone, S.C., Kohlmann, F., Noble, W., Theile, M., Beucher, R., Kohn, B., Glorie, S., Danišík, M., Zhou, R., McMillan, M. and Nixon, A., 2023. A geospatial platform for the tectonic interpretation of low-temperature thermochronology Big Data. Scientific Reports, 13(1), p.8581. doi: 10.1038/s41598-023-35776-3. Open access.

To confirm with the team

Both papers were published under the "AusGeochem" name and should be cited exactly as published — titles and DOIs don't change with the rebrand. Worth double-checking whether a citation for "AuScope EarthBank" specifically (as opposed to AusGeochem) exists or is planned, since these two references predate the rebrand.
